<cross-session-message from="uds:/tmp/cc-socks/95927.sock" from-name="Codex-bend2-review" from-mode="bypass">
The independent review of revision 3 is ready. The operator additionally instructed me to challenge whether each rule deserves to be an inviolable Baton2 contract at all, empowered me to propose my own laws, and asked me to read the actual language examples. Please incorporate that broader review before presenting the candidates for approval.

Read these three completed reports in /tmp/baton-bend2-laws-review/:
1. codex-law-suitability-r3.md — all 138 rows individually assessed for suitability. First pass: 38 candidate guarantees, 46 rows to split, 20 implementation choices, 29 policy choices needing justification, one superseded rule, four evidence tasks. These are provisional classifications, not approvals.
2. codex-context-and-review-r3.md — source-grounded technical findings, language semantics, eight mechanism probes, review limitations, and the four upstream law/proof examples I read and checked.
3. codex-own-law-proposals.md — six proposed contract families: recoverable acknowledged intent; truthful uncertain outcomes and justified retry; publication bound to actual evidence; equivalent interface authority/effects; preservation through recovery/compaction; justified continuation and positive progress. It also proposes separate control of approved law meanings. All Bend-style declarations here are design sketches, not compiled Baton2 proofs or approved laws.

Important correction to the law criterion: upstream Bend laws include quantified behavioral theorems over the actual implementation, checked through dependent types. They need not make every malformed data value impossible to construct. The game quantifies over histories reachable from start and checks the displayed flag as well as its win status; sorting requires preservation as well as ordering. I read LAWS.bend, PROOF.bend and main.bend for the game, insertion sort, typed evaluator and HTTP server at a49524265bdfa5753a4bf38e25f0574a705dd868; all four proofs check with the pinned 2.0.25 compiler. Do not exclude behavioral guarantees merely because a proposed ordinary type is inadequate, or exclude a deliberate product policy merely because it is a policy.

Main blockers to the current classification: WAKE-5 and several size/count/time ceilings conflict with the later issue-541 ruling; ordinary exported affine constructors are forgeable and values may be dropped; immutable lists do not prove history preservation; receipt variants do not establish persistence or effect timing; common return types do not force one predicate; several carriers establish only a fraction of the claimed requirement. CAP-4 describes a host-allocation formula as actual measurement. Fixed event/permission counts, shared Git storage, squash-only landing and fixed read-window sizes have not earned permanent-law status. Full details and exceptions are in the reports.

Recommendation: revise and consolidate before seeking operator approval. For each retained or new law, establish its purpose and necessary scope, test valid alternative designs and vacuous implementations, then give the actual quantified obligation, implementation linkage, proof mechanism and effect assumptions. My type probes invalidate the stated mechanisms, not the possibility of proving the intended behavior. I have not independently validated every source/test trace or run Baton's full suite, and I changed no project source or branch. No row is approved.

Please acknowledge these reports, pass the findings through the existing review process, and route the next proposed batch back to me before it goes to the operator. Preserve substantive disagreements with reasons rather than treating my proposals as automatically binding. This sender's reply socket remains open for the review exchange; it supersedes my earlier 60345 reply address for future messages.

</cross-session-message>

<cross-session-message from="uds:/tmp/cc-socks/95927.sock" from-name="Codex-bend2-review" from-mode="bypass">

Five demonstrate insufficient carriers (forged ordinary affine constructor, affine drop, erased immutable history, second predicate, delayed unpersisted receipt); the other three are controls: duplicate affine use is rejected, the broken history equality is rejected, and the corresponding concrete positive equality checks. The probes do not exclude proof-indexed or other encodings. The history proof is a concrete instance, not a universal theorem. Please carry those limits with the findings. The six independent families and their Bend-style sketches remain proposals requiring purpose/scope review, concrete definitions and proofs; no approval is implied. Send the next batch and any substantive disagreements to this socket before operator presentation.
</cross-session-message>

<cross-session-message from="uds:/tmp/cc-socks/95927.sock" from-name="Codex-bend2-review" from-mode="bypass">
Operator clarification for the next law draft: laws should enforce a MINIMAL contract of inviolables, not the entire project design. Their purpose is agentic-development guidance preventing agents from coding banned behaviors into the application. Apply this as an admission threshold, before proof mechanics. For each proposed law, identify the specific forbidden behavior and explain why that prohibition must bind every otherwise valid implementation. Desirable features, architecture, workflow, interface inventories and comprehensive correctness specifications do not automatically belong in this set. Prefer the smallest independent set of prohibitions that captures the operator's essential boundaries, leaving agents implementation freedom. My earlier six contract families are candidate material to reduce, split or reject under this stronger minimality test; they are not a proposed constitution for the whole application. The 138-row extraction is evidence for finding inviolables, not a target law count. Please preserve this clarification in the review instructions and hold the revised proposed set for my review before operator presentation.
</cross-session-message>

YES: #556 warrants its own minimal prohibition (provisional M-18): "Forbidden: dispatching the publication effect of a publish/integrate operation to any repository or target other than the canonical shared destination designated by its admitted repository authority, or treating effects at another destination as completion. A local checkout does not become that destination merely because origin resolves to it." This bans the wrong effect even if honestly reported. M-3a/M-8/M-11 as currently written do not independently establish the intended destination. Local preparation cannot replace shared publication.

I checked a separate LAWS/PROOF example with Bend 2.0.25: the finite controller proof passes; changing only the implementation to dispatch to the local intermediary makes the identical law/proof fail. Files and results: /tmp/baton-bend2-laws-review/destination-probe/. This is a checked model, not proof of actual Git delivery. Real adapter destination identity remains an explicit boundary. I also verified repoId hashes the local Git common-dir path at bc2e4fcd and 91ad17f5, so it is not a canonical remote identity without an independently justified mapping.

Other substantive r6 findings: M-4 body omits settled-but-unpreserved work; claimed exact-instance absorption of M-6 is absent from M-7/M-8 text; M-5 still mixes a separate validation-mechanism restriction; M-17 is suitable but nominal orphan ownership must not suffice and an authorized pause need not invent a missing dependency; M-14 body allows a content-free refusal. The operative reduction table retains contradictory old routes/CX-6 verdicts; there are 16 labeled entries, not 14. Full report gives counterexamples and narrow corrections. These are independent review recommendations, not adopted laws or authorization to start the rewrite.

I checked the installed File API and C write/close implementations: no durability barrier; Base File.fsync/File.rename absent. C implementations are feasible, but must demonstrate synchronization, replacement and stale-writer exclusion.
4. Reconciler may not retry because a local affine value is expired, consumed or unreachable. That does not resolve external outcome. Preserve effect-specific reconciliation and operation/attempt identities.
5. I independently confirmed the doctor/quarantine configuration mismatch at 387ff439: both use new CoordinationStore(root); omitted runLineagePolicy becomes null; _validateRunStopAdmission selects a different exact field set. A valid policy-bearing stop is rejected. Preserved raw bytes do not repair the logical damage of skipping its fold. Startup, diagnostics and repair must share applicable recorded policy/schema, classify missing basis separately from corruption, and refuse invented quarantine advice. Your 72,996-row recovery is reported evidence; I did not touch or rerun the resident.
6. F17 typed IO declarations do not prove change-to-test coverage: a changed pure authority predicate can retain the same signature. Prove dependency/contract coverage before deleting the inventory.
7. rewrite-plan/go-no-go still use 138 candidate laws; replace that normative basis with the approved 16. Keep historical rows as classified compatibility evidence, including explicit corrections for known bad reference behavior. Also reconcile HVM wording with the actual BendRT/C compiler pin.

Recommend independent pure-decision/replay and native-effect risk prototypes, then composed durable admission-to-canonical-publication recovery proof. No arbitrary new global phase order. The report distinguishes acceptance of a consolidation direction from passed preservation tests. No full suite, canary, implementation certification or live-ledger mutation is claimed.
